summary: A lightweight object-component placeholder used for grouping transforms, look-at targets, camera/light focus points, and bone-chain end affectors in 3D scene hierarchies.

key_params.name: xord
key_params.note: Transform order for translate, rotate, and scale

key_params.name: p
key_params.note: Pivot point for scale and rotation

key_params.name: lookat
key_params.note: Object this Null or child object should face

key_params.name: pathsop
key_params.note: Path for moving the component along a curve

key_concepts: Null COMP is a scene placeholder object for transforming attached components without adding visible geometry.
It is the standard invisible target for Look At workflows, including camera and light center-of-interest controls.
It can act as a bone-chain end affector when rigging object hierarchies.
Xform parameters such as transform order, rotate order, translate, rotate, scale, pivot, and parent transform source determine final object placement.
Path SOP, Orient Along Path, up-vector, and auto-bank controls let a Null COMP drive path-following motion for cameras or other components.
common_gotchas: Null COMP has no visible geometry by default; it is mainly a transform and hierarchy helper.
Look At behavior can flip or animate poorly when the target crosses the up vector; choose an appropriate up-vector mode.
Transform order and rotation order materially change final placement.
Pivot changes can make scaling and rotation appear to slide the object.
Use a Null COMP as a camera or light focus target when the target itself should not render.
As a bone end affector, keep transform parenting clean so the IK setup receives predictable target positions.
build_relevance: 2021.10000+ object hierarchy transforms and look-at targets
